quote: GF guide states the food is 「完全に独立した厨房で調理されており、グルテンフリーの安全性を確認しています」 (cooked in a completely independent kitchen, gluten-free safety confirmed).
found: しかし、このお店は完全に独立した厨房で調理されており、グルテンフリーの安全性を確保しています。
note: Wording is 安全性を確保 (ensured), not 確認 (confirmed) — fix the quote. Also: this is the content-farm author's own assertion reasoning from the parent bakery's flour dust, not a statement by the shop; the shop's own site carries no such claim.

quote: Operator claim: 「すべてのメニューがグルテンフリー」— no wheat flour anywhere; udon is 玄米 (brown rice) and fry batter is 米粉 (rice flour), so the fryer handles only GF batter.
found: 当店は、すべてのメニューがグルテンフリーで、京都の食材を多く使い、ランチで提供する「うどん」は玄米、揚げ物の衣も米粉を使ったグルテンフリーに仕上げました。
note: Quote verbatim. But the trailing inference 'so the fryer handles only GF batter' is the record's own — the release contains neither 厨房 nor 調味料 and says nothing about the fryer; drop or re-source that clause.

quote: GF guide notes 「小麦不使用の調味料を厳選」 (wheat-free condiments carefully selected), indicating tamari-style / wheat-free soy and tsuyu.
found: Table row: 定食のおかず ｜ 小麦不使用の調味料を厳選
note: The phrase is a table cell scoped to 定食のおかず (teishoku side dishes) only — not a whole-kitchen condiment policy — and the page never mentions tamari, soy sauce or tsuyu. The 'indicating tamari-style soy and tsuyu' gloss is unsourced inference on a celiac-critical point.

quote: Dashi is a traditional bonito (かつお)/kombu stock and egg is used widely; only the kombu-water salad udon is flagged plant-based, so vegan cross-contact with fish stock is likely across most dishes.
found: 「ヴィーガンの方におすすめな『昆布水サラダうどん』」 / 「だし巻き卵は蘭王たまごを贅沢に使い、お出汁たっぷりの豊かな風味を楽しんで。」
note: The page supports the egg-heavy and vegan-udon halves, but かつお/bonito appears NOWHERE on it — the fish-stock attribution that drives the whole vegan verdict is invented for this citation. The article only ever writes 出汁/お出汁 with no ingredient named.

quote: GF guide advises: 「グルテンフリー以外のアレルギーがある場合は、事前にお店へ確認してください」 (for allergies other than gluten, confirm with the shop in advance).
found: ・グルテンフリー以外のアレルギー（乳・卵など）がある場合は、事前にお店へ確認してください。
note: Quote silently drops （乳・卵など）; restore it. Substance intact.

quote: Whole menu is gluten-free with a separate/independent kitchen — a rare celiac-safe sit-down option in the Arashiyama tourist core.
found: 「特に『和レ和レ和 アラシヤマ』『玄gen』『cafe planet』は全メニューがグルテンフリーのため、小麦アレルギーのお子さんでも安心して食事ができます。ただし、事前に電話やメールでアレルギーの詳細を伝えておくことをおすすめします。また、重度のアレルギーの場合は、コンタミネーション（交差汚染）への対応状況も確認しておくと安心です。」
note: QUOTE CUT BEFORE ITS OWN ただし EXCEPTION. The page's FAQ tells severe-allergy diners to go and verify the shop's cross-contamination handling themselves — the opposite of 'celiac-safe'; it frames the shop as 小麦アレルギーのお子さん-friendly and never says celiac-safe. With the Oct-2024 nhkomorebi first-hand report of 小麦入りの白だし already logged in gf_detail, this positive should be struck.

quote: Run by an established 32-store café group (パンとエスプレッソと / 株式会社日と々と), suggesting consistent operating standards.
found: 表参道のベーカリーカフェ「パンとエスプレッソと」をはじめ、国内に32店舗展開する株式会社日と々と（東京都渋谷区神宮前/代表取締役 山本拓三）は…
note: 32 domestic stores confirmed verbatim; the scale is the parent group's, not the GF concept's (Arashiyama is only the 2nd 和レ和レ和).

quote: The shop says it uses dedicated pots and utensils to minimize cross-contamination for gluten-free guests, but it is a shared kitchen that also cooks standard wheat ramen, so it is not a fully dedicated gluten-free environment.
found: FMGF owner statement: "Separate Preparation Areas: Our gluten-free dishes are prepared using dedicated cookware, utensils, and strainers to prevent cross-contamination. Dedicated Water: We boil our gluten-free noodles in fresh, dedicated water—never in the same water used for regular wheat noodles. Carefully Sourced Ingredients: We use gluten-free tamari/soy sauce and thoroughly inspect all seasonings and ingredients to guarantee they are safe."
method: 1 plain+mobile UA, 3 Wayback 2025-01-22, 4 Yahoo Japan exact-phrase search
note: fireramen.com's HTML contains no occurrence of 'dedicated', 'utensil', 'cross-contamination' or 'rice flour', and neither does the 2025-01 Wayback capture; the exact phrase 'to minimize cross-contamination' returns nothing for Menbaka on Yahoo Japan. The claim is TRUE and well evidenced — but at the FMGF owner statement, not the official site. Caveat: the site's FAQ answer 'How do you handle Gluten-Free orders?' is a JS-only Wix accordion body that plain fetch, r.jina.ai browser engine and Wayback all returned empty.

quote: The regular menu is a soy-sauce (shoyu) ramen; standard shoyu tare is typically wheat-based. The gluten-free version is a separate reservation-only preparation rather than the default bowl.
found: "we focus on preserving the traditional taste of Shoyu Ramen—a soy sauce-based broth that is light yet deeply flavorful" — but also 「Walk in Course Menu （Vegetarian, Muslim friendly, Gluten free available）」
note: First half supported. Second half is CONTRADICTED by the same page: the Walk in Course Menu, not only the two reservation courses, is labelled '（Vegetarian, Muslim friendly, Gluten free available）'. GF is not reservation-only. The record also omits that the FMGF owner statement says GF bowls use gluten-free tamari — the single most useful fact for a celiac here.

quote: Vegan orders are marked with a colored number card placed at the seat so staff serve the correct plant-based bowl, but the shop does not publish details on separate cooking surfaces for vegan items.
found: "When you order the vegan menu, a green number card is placed in front of your seat to ensure flawless service for those who have chosen the vegan option."
note: Supported; the card is specifically green — say so. The 'no published separate surfaces' half is fair: the page is silent on it.

quote: Gluten-free, vegan, vegetarian and no-pork (Muslim-friendly) bowls are offered as a reservation-only special set menu booked in advance via TableCheck; the regular walk-in menu cannot be swapped for these, so dietary guests should reserve ahead and state needs clearly.
found: "For reservation system we only have the SPECIAL SET MENU and it's NOT POSSIBLE to change it for a regular menu. Regular menu is only for walk-in customers." — and separately 「Walk in Course Menu （Vegetarian, Muslim friendly, Gluten free available）」
note: MATERIAL MISREADING of the cited sentence. The site means a RESERVATION cannot be downgraded to the regular menu — not that dietary bowls require a reservation. The page marks the Walk in Course Menu as Vegetarian/Muslim-friendly/Gluten-free available, and an FMGF reviewer describes walking in without a booking and eating GF fire ramen after a 45-minute wait.

quote: Rare among ramen shops, this kitchen intentionally caters to gluten-free, vegan, vegetarian and Muslim-friendly diners, with premium rice-flour noodles for gluten-free guests and a fully plant-based vegan fire ramen offered since 2020.
found: fireramen.com: "we now proudly offer vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, and Muslim-friendly options". FMGF owner statement: "fully Gluten-Free Ramen options prepared with 100% gluten-free noodles… Vegan & Gluten-Free options are also available!" fireramen.com/menu JSON: "Vegetable Ramen — A 100% plant-based ramen crafted from a delicate broth of kombu, dried daikon, and shiitake."
method: 1 plain+mobile UA, plus the Wix menu JSON behind /menu, plus r.jina.ai for FMGF
note: The four-diet sentence is supported. 'premium RICE-FLOUR noodles' is not — neither the official site nor the owner statement says rice flour; the owner says only '100% gluten-free noodles'. 'since 2020' appears on neither. Both specifics need a real source or removal.

quote: English website, English-speaking staff and online reservations make it straightforward for foreign diners to arrange and confirm special dietary bowls before visiting.
found: fooddiversity says the opposite on reservations — "Reservation: No need/unavailable" — and says nothing about English. Real support: fireramen.com is entirely in English and links https://www.tablecheck.com/en/shops/menbaka/reserve; FMGF review (5 days ago, Gluten Sensitive): "The staff were amazing, and were able to understand English".
method: 1 plain fetch of both; FMGF via r.jina.ai
note: Claim is true but cited to a page that flatly contradicts its reservation half. Re-point at fireramen.com (TableCheck link) plus the FMGF reviews.
